metadata.method: Dated original records with second-publisher review; source independence and storm segment denominators noted; no automated editorial approval.
metadata.editorial_qc_note: Initial March 11 1888 Blizzard candidate withdrawn because March 12 already covers the same blizzard. Also replaced Feb13 1899 outbreak and Mar15 Idai repetition with distinct dated events; all superseded selections retained for historical audit.

reviews.title_after: An EF3 tornado tears through West Liberty during Kentucky's March outbreak
reviews.location_after: West Liberty and eastern Morgan County, Kentucky
reviews.evidence_independence: NCEI Artville/Morgan County segment and NWS Jackson reconstruction derive from the same NWS damage survey; a second URL is not independent tornado-wind measurement
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: On March 2, 2012, the West Liberty EF3 tornado moved from Menifee County through Morgan County, Kentucky; the original Artville NCEI entry is a segment of this long-track tornado.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Do not count the Artville/Morgan segment as an additional separate EF3 tornado or combine entire outbreak casualties with this track. NWS lists a wider 86-mile path across Kentucky and West Virginia; exact survey bounds, EF3 points, and fatality denominators require review.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original map comparing the surveyed West Liberty path with county/segment boundaries and local warning chronology

reviews.title_after: Cyclone Pam strengthens as Vanuatu prepares for a dangerous Pacific storm
reviews.location_after: Between the Solomon Islands, Vanuatu and Fiji, South Pacific
reviews.second_source_publisher: Secretariat of the Pacific Regional Environment Programme
reviews.evidence_independence: Dated independent March 11 media reporting cites tropical forecasting agencies; regional intergovernmental disaster chronology independently documents subsequent Vanuatu impacts but both depend on agency cyclone intensity analysis
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: On March 11, 2015, contemporaneous reporting documented Tropical Cyclone Pam intensifying to Category 3 near waters between Vanuatu and Fiji, with warnings for Vanuatu ahead of its later March 13–14 impacts.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Do NOT claim Pam struck Vanuatu on March 11. The March 11 contemporaneous Category 3 description uses its reporting agency's scale and date; Pam's Category 5 strength and Vanuatu passage occurred later. Distinguish Fiji/Solomon Islands warnings from eventual Vanuatu impacts, and review regional wind-averaging conventions.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original March 9–14 Pam intensity and forecast-cone timeline with March 11 warning status and later Vanuatu crossing dated separately
reviews.editorial_reason: Replaces adjacent duplicate historic storm with distinct event without changing any fact check or publishing gate.

reviews.title_after: A family of tornadoes devastates Comfrey and St. Peter, Minnesota
reviews.evidence_independence: State Climatology Office independently catalogs the March tornado family but historical tornado tracks and rating assessments share NWS/Weather Bureau source material
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: The March 29, 1998 southern Minnesota tornado outbreak heavily damaged Comfrey and St. Peter. The original NCEI Comfrey location describes part of a long-track tornado.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The DNR refers to a family of 13 tornadoes; the NCEI Comfrey line is only one individual track. The outbreak count, distinct tornado ratings and Comfrey versus St. Peter casualties must not be conflated.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original individual tornado-track sequence that keeps Comfrey/St. Peter storm paths and county segments separate

reviews.title_after: An EF3 tornado strikes Onalaska on the shore of Lake Livingston
reviews.location_after: Onalaska and Paradise Acres, Polk County, eastern Texas
reviews.evidence_independence: NCEI Polk County entry and detailed NWS Houston tornado page are generated from the same damage survey; radar and satellite observations provide complementary, not fully independent, event evidence
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: An EF3 tornado struck the Onalaska/Lake Livingston area in Texas on April 22, 2020, causing major damage in the Paradise Acres community.
reviews.unverified_cautions: A 140 mph EF3 maximum is a damage-survey estimate, not a measured on-site anemometer gust. Distinguish radar signatures and surveyed damage; do not reuse local storm photographs until specific permissions or rights are confirmed.
reviews.graphic_concept: Redraw the official Polk County tornado path and sequence of radar velocity scans, with surveyed EF3 damage marked separately

reviews.title_after: The Great Natchez Tornado devastates boats and riverfront communities
reviews.location_after: Concordia Parish, Louisiana, and Natchez, Mississippi
reviews.evidence_independence: NWS Jackson historical comparison and a separate historical-journalism synthesis both depend on archival nineteenth-century reports; modern fatality rankings derive from overlapping tornado catalogs
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: On May 7, 1840, a powerful tornado followed the Mississippi River from the Louisiana side toward Natchez, devastating boats and riverfront areas.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The oft-quoted 317 deaths is a historical estimate with likely incomplete enumeration, especially among enslaved people; do not imply exact verified casualty census. Do not apply a modern EF rating to this pre-Fujita event or borrow drawings without provenance.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Mississippi River channel-and-port map highlighting Natchez, Concordia/Vidalia and documented damage zones, clearly marking the historical path as approximate

reviews.title_after: The Westfield–Springfield EF3 tornado crosses the Connecticut River
reviews.location_after: Westfield, Springfield and surrounding southwestern Massachusetts
reviews.evidence_independence: The NCEI Westfield Hampden County segment and NWS Boston StoryMap share official tornado survey origins; historical reanalysis and surface/radar imagery provide supplemental observational context
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: An EF3 tornado struck western Massachusetts on June 1, 2011, tracking from near Westfield across the Connecticut River into Springfield and continuing eastward.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Do not confuse the Hampden County NCEI section with total tornado path or additional Massachusetts tornadoes. The early NWS public-information statement was preliminary; 160 mph refers to damage-based EF-scale estimate, not measured gust.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Connecticut River crossing diagram and west-to-east path/transect with time annotations from dated radar and official survey

reviews.title_after: Tropical Storm Allison forms just offshore of Texas before its devastating flood legacy
reviews.location_after: Northwestern Gulf of Mexico and upper Texas coast near Galveston
reviews.evidence_independence: NHC advisory/best-track source and NCEI Harris County storm account are two NOAA datasets; no independent observation is implied by the separate URLs
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: Tropical Storm Allison formed over the northwestern Gulf on June 5, 2001 and approached the upper Texas coast later that day; its catastrophic Houston-area flooding occurred over the ensuing days.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Some NOAA retrospective accounts date initial landfall late June 5 near Freeport, whereas the NCEI Harris County narrative describes the west end of Galveston Island around midnight June 5–6. Confirm landfall location/clock with NHC best track before stating a single exact time. June 8–9 Houston rainfall totals must NOT be attributed to June 5.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original June 5 formation/first Texas coast approach timeline with subsequent June 6–9 rain episodes shown in separately dated panels

reviews.title_after: An overnight flash flood overwhelms the Albert Pike Recreation Area
reviews.location_after: Upper Little Missouri River, Montgomery County, Arkansas
reviews.evidence_independence: USGS hydraulic field investigation estimates independent peak discharges from postflood high-water marks; event narrative also uses rainfall/radar observations shared with NWS
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: In the early hours of June 11, 2010, catastrophic flash flooding affected the Albert Pike Recreation Area along the Little Missouri River in southwest Arkansas.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The 40,100 cfs peak is a USGS indirect hydraulic estimate near Albert Pike, not a direct in-stream peak meter reading at every affected campsite. A 1:57 AM warning issuance, fatalities and nighttime warning availability have separate scopes needing verification.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original river-catchment and rainfall-to-stage flood chronology with separately labeled USGS indirect peak estimate

reviews.original_title: Dust Storm — EASTERN JUAB/MILLARD COUNTIES, Utah
reviews.title_after: Thunderstorm outflow whips up a blinding dust storm on Interstate 15 near Kanosh
reviews.location_after: Interstate 15 near Kanosh, Millard County, Utah
reviews.second_source_publisher: KSL News reporting Utah Highway Patrol
reviews.evidence_independence: Contemporaneous independent newsroom coverage of police reports supports the collision/date; NCEI meteorological report and news share highway-patrol crash records, not measured visibility data
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: On July 25, 2021, thunderstorm outflow generated dense blowing dust across I-15 near Kanosh, Utah, contributing to a major multi-vehicle crash.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Immediate reports gave varying death and vehicle totals; later Utah Highway Patrol reporting used 8 fatalities and 22 vehicles. Attribute final totals to the responsible agency; near-zero visibility is inferred from reports, not a sustained point anemometer reading.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original I-15 corridor and convective-outflow map with measured nearby wind and dust-visibility reports distinguished

reviews.title_after: The College Park F3 tornado rips across Maryland's University of Maryland corridor
reviews.evidence_independence: Peer-reviewed satellite/radar environmental analysis distinct from original NCEI county survey, though tornado path and damage ratings still use prior NOAA/NWS observational sources
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: An F3 tornado tracked through the College Park area of Maryland on September 24, 2001; the NCEI Hyattsville entry marks an initial portion of the longer tornado.
reviews.unverified_cautions: This is an F3 (pre-2007 Fujita scale), not EF3. The journal identifies the College Park tornado as one of three tornadoes from the broader supercell; do not conflate its track with earlier separate tornadoes. The article's CC BY paper license does not automatically clear every embedded third-party figure.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original radar-animation-derived storm-relative path and college/Route 1 geographic overlay with survey track separate from broader supercell

reviews.title_after: The Saxby Gale floods New Brunswick's Bay of Fundy coastline
reviews.location_after: Bay of Fundy, Saint John, Moncton and Sackville, New Brunswick, Canada
reviews.second_source_publisher: Albert County Museum & R.B. Bennett Centre
reviews.evidence_independence: New Brunswick governmental flood register and regional museum independently compile historical records, but share recollections and 1869 newspaper sources
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: A major windstorm and exceptional tidal flooding affected New Brunswick on October 4–5, 1869, known as the Saxby Gale; the disaster includes storm and tide effects continuing into October 5.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Event began October 4, not exclusively October 5. Saxby's astronomical forecast was not a scientifically reliable storm forecast; do not imply he physically predicted synoptic cyclone track. Coastal damage and historically quoted water levels need tidal datum/source verification.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Bay of Fundy high-tide funneling schematic and Oct 4–5 coastal impact chronology with dated place labels

reviews.title_after: The Cedar Fire ignites as Santa Ana winds set up a wildfire disaster near San Diego
reviews.location_after: Cleveland National Forest east of San Diego, California
reviews.second_source_publisher: City of San Diego Fire-Rescue Department
reviews.evidence_independence: San Diego municipal incident history independently confirms the initial reported fire date and local impacts; NOAA/NCEI weather narrative supplies independent meteorological context but shares incident reports
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: The Cedar Fire was reported on the evening of October 25, 2003, east of San Diego. Santa Ana winds helped it expand rapidly during October 26.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Most catastrophic urban impacts occurred October 26, not October 25. The reported start time, cause and final acres differ among incident histories; avoid unsourced record rankings (other California fires later exceeded Cedar). Rights to historic fire photos not automatically public-domain.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original two-day October 25 ignition and October 26 Santa Ana wind/fire-perimeter evolution using agency timestamps

reviews.original_title: Wildfire — GREATER RENO/CARSON CITY/MINDEN AREA, Nevada
reviews.title_after: Powerful downslope winds drive Reno's destructive Caughlin Fire
reviews.location_after: Caughlin Ranch and southwest Reno, Nevada
reviews.evidence_independence: Contemporaneous local report independently confirms fire date/response; NCEI wildfire narrative and local reporting depend in part on county fire/utility officials for ignition/evacuation claims
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: On November 18, 2011, strong downslope winds along the Sierra Front fueled the rapidly spreading Caughlin Fire in southwest Reno, Nevada.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The wind fueled the fire; do not say wind itself caused ignition, which was traced to utility/electrical incident. Regional 80-mph gusts are not necessarily measured at the ignition spot; the Nevada Climate Office quarterly summary references broader Sierra Front winds, not local fire-front speed.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Reno foothill topography and downslope wind/fire growth timeline using independently sourced wind reports and incident updates

reviews.title_after: A violent EF4 tornado sweeps from Holly Springs toward Ashland, Mississippi
reviews.location_after: Holly Springs–Ashland corridor, northern Mississippi into southwestern Tennessee
reviews.evidence_independence: NCEI Ashland county track section and NWS Memphis full-track reconstruction rely on the same final NWS tornado survey, not independent rated-wind measurement
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: On December 23, 2015, a violent EF4 tornado crossed parts of northern Mississippi including the Holly Springs–Ashland corridor and continued toward southwest Tennessee.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The NWS explicitly split an earlier long apparent damage swath into TWO tornadoes. The original NCEI Benton County record is only a piece of tornado #3; avoid assigning all outbreak fatalities or EF4 damage uniformly along the entire track.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original split-track survey diagram highlighting tornado #3's Holly Springs–Ashland path, distinct from adjacent tornado #2

reviews.original_title: The Great Arctic Outbreak of February 1899
reviews.title_after: Ex-Tropical Cyclone Gabrielle lashes New Zealand's northern North Island
reviews.location_after: Northland, Auckland and the northern North Island of New Zealand
reviews.evidence_independence: MetService's operational track and NIWA's retrospective use overlapping meteorological observations, but NIWA separately describes regional impacts and rainfall; two institutional URLs are not independent coastal anemometer readings
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: Ex-Tropical Cyclone Gabrielle was passing close to New Zealand's northern North Island on February 13, 2023, producing dangerous wind and rain; severe impacts continued February 14.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Gabrielle was an ex-tropical cyclone near New Zealand, not a Category 5 tropical cyclone at Auckland. Local emergency declarations occurred February 13; the national state of emergency was not declared until February 14. Do not move peak rainfall or the February 14 national declaration backward a day.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Feb 13 storm-track versus North Island rainfall/wind warning timeline with the Feb 14 national emergency distinguished
reviews.editorial_reason: Replaces adjacent duplicate historic storm with distinct event without changing any fact check or publishing gate.

reviews.title_after: Rapid snowmelt and rain drive historic Nebraska river flooding
reviews.location_after: Platte, Elkhorn and Loup River basins, central and eastern Nebraska
reviews.evidence_independence: NWS Hastings regional flood chronology and NOAA GOES-R satellite imagery are different observational products but share NOAA institutional origin; satellite flood extent does not independently validate specific river gauge crests
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: On March 15, 2019, historic flooding spread across Nebraska river basins after heavy rain and rapid snowmelt over frozen ground; NOAA GOES imagery captured extensive inundation that day.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The flooding developed March 13–17, and many specific river gauge peaks occurred on later dates. Do not assign the entire multiday disaster, record crest at Nebraska City or annual economic toll to March 15. Distinguish satellite water footprint from river gauge stages and ice-jam effects.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original March 15 GOES flood extent and river network graphic, separating dated discharge crest times from satellite scene time
reviews.editorial_reason: Replaces adjacent duplicate historic storm with distinct event without changing any fact check or publishing gate.
